title: Volcano Islands
blurb: Why does the ground rumble in Indonesia, and what comes out of a volcano? Find out how mountains can breathe fire.

chapters.title: A Mountain with a Fire Inside
chapters.text:
A volcano is a place where hot melted rock comes out of the Earth. Most volcanoes look like mountains, with a bowl-shaped opening at the top called a crater.

To understand a volcano, think about the Earth as an egg. The thin outside is the crust, like the shell. We live on it. Our homes, seas and forests all sit on this thin shell. Under the crust is a thick layer called the mantle, like the egg white. The mantle is so hot that some rock in it melts. In the very middle is the core, like the yolk. The core is the hottest part of all.

Melted rock under the ground is called magma. When magma pushes out of a volcano, we call it lava. It is the same hot rock with a new name. Lava is bright orange and much hotter than any oven at home. It becomes hard, black rock when it cools down.

Each time a volcano erupts, new rock and ash pile up around the opening. Over thousands of years, the pile grows into a mountain. So a volcano really builds itself.

Mount Merapi, in Central Java, is one of the busiest volcanoes in Indonesia. Its name means mountain of fire.

questions.prompt: What is a volcano?
options: A very tall mountain that has snow on its top
A deep hole that was made by a falling rock
A place where hot melted rock comes out of the Earth
A deep lake of cold water at the top of a mountain
questions.why: The first sentence says a volcano is a place where hot melted rock comes out of the Earth.

questions.prompt: What is the bowl-shaped opening at the top of a volcano called?
options: A cave
A crater
A valley
A tunnel
questions.why: The bowl-shaped opening at the top is called a crater.

questions.prompt: In the egg picture, which part of the egg is like the Earth's crust?
options: The white
The air inside
The yolk
The shell
questions.why: The thin outside is the crust, like the shell.

questions.prompt: Which part of the Earth is the hottest?
options: The core
The crust
The mantle
The lava
questions.why: The core is in the very middle, and the text calls it the hottest part of all.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between magma and lava?
options: Magma is under the ground, and lava has come out
Magma is in the sea, and lava is on the land
Magma is cold rock, and lava is hot rock
Magma is black, and lava is always white
questions.why: Melted rock under the ground is called magma. When it pushes out of a volcano, we call it lava.

questions.prompt: How does a volcano grow into a mountain?
options: The crust folds up slowly in the hot sun
Rivers carry sand to the top of the crater
New rock and ash pile up each time it erupts
The plants on its sides grow taller every year
questions.why: Each time a volcano erupts, new rock and ash pile up around the opening, and over thousands of years the pile grows into a mountain.

questions.prompt: What does the name Merapi mean?
options: Child of the sea
Mountain of fire
Mountain of snow
Home of the wind
questions.why: The text says the name Merapi means mountain of fire.

chapters.title: Why So Many in Indonesia?
chapters.text:
Indonesia has more than one hundred active volcanoes. That is a lot for one country. Why?

The Earth's crust is not one piece. It is broken into huge slabs called plates, like a cracked eggshell. The plates move very slowly all the time, about as fast as your fingernails grow. Sometimes one plate slides under another. When this happens, rock goes down into the hot mantle and melts. The new magma rises and finds a way out. This is how many volcanoes are born.

Moving plates can also stick together and then suddenly jerk. Then the ground shakes, and we call it an earthquake.

Indonesia sits where several plates meet. It is part of a long curve of volcanoes and earthquakes around the Pacific Ocean. People call this curve the Ring of Fire.

One famous volcano stands in the sea between Java and Sumatra. It is called Krakatau. In 1883, it blew up with a bang so loud that people heard it thousands of kilometres away. Much of the island disappeared. But the story did not end there. Years later, in 1927, a new volcano rose out of the same sea. People named it Anak Krakatau, which means child of Krakatau.

questions.prompt: How many active volcanoes does Indonesia have?
options: About thirty
More than one hundred
Fewer than ten
Exactly one
questions.why: The first sentence says Indonesia has more than one hundred active volcanoes.

questions.prompt: What are the huge slabs of the Earth's crust called?
options: Plates
Craters
Shells
Layers
questions.why: The crust is broken into huge slabs called plates.

questions.prompt: How fast do the plates move?
options: They do not move at all
About as fast as a person can walk
About as fast as your fingernails grow
About as fast as a car on the road
questions.why: The plates move very slowly, about as fast as your fingernails grow.

questions.prompt: What can happen when one plate slides under another?
options: A new forest grows on top of the plates
The two plates join to make one big plate
The sea above it dries up very quickly
Rock goes down into the mantle and melts
questions.why: When one plate slides under another, rock goes down into the hot mantle and melts.

questions.prompt: What makes the ground shake in an earthquake?
options: Rain falls on the side of a tall mountain
The core of the Earth starts to go cold
Lava cools down and turns into black rock
Plates stick together and then suddenly jerk
questions.why: Moving plates can stick together and then suddenly jerk. Then the ground shakes.

questions.prompt: Why does Indonesia have so many volcanoes?
options: It is very close to a desert
It is a very hot country
It sits where several plates meet
It has more rain than other countries
questions.why: The chapter asks why and then explains that volcanoes form where plates move, and that Indonesia sits where several plates meet.

questions.prompt: What is Anak Krakatau?
options: A scientist who studied Krakatau for years
A new volcano that rose from the sea in 1927
A name for the Ring of Fire in Indonesia
A town that was built near Krakatau in 1883
questions.why: Years later, in 1927, a new volcano rose out of the same sea. People named it Anak Krakatau.

chapters.title: When a Volcano Erupts
chapters.text:
Deep inside a volcano, magma slowly collects in a big space called a magma chamber. The magma holds gas, like the bubbles in a bottle of fizzy drink. As more magma arrives, the pressure grows. Think of shaking that bottle before you open it.

When the pressure is too high, the volcano erupts. Lava may flow down the side. Hot ash and small rocks may shoot into the air. This ash is made of tiny pieces of rock and glass. It makes a thick grey cloud that can reach high into the sky and fall far away.

Not every eruption is the same. Some are quiet, with slow rivers of lava. Others are loud and sudden. Sometimes a hot cloud of ash and gas rushes down the mountain, faster than a car on the road. People near Merapi call this cloud wedhus gembel, which means shaggy goat in Javanese, because of its curly grey shape.

The biggest eruption ever recorded was Tambora, on the island of Sumbawa, in 1815. Its ash and gas blocked some of the sunlight, and the next summer was very cold in Europe.

Scientists called volcanologists watch the mountain with special tools. They measure tiny shakes in the ground and the gas in the air.

questions.prompt: Where does magma collect inside a volcano?
options: In the crater at the top
In a tunnel to the core
In a river under the sea
In a magma chamber
questions.why: Magma collects in a big space called a magma chamber.

questions.prompt: Why does the text talk about a shaken bottle of fizzy drink?
options: Volcanoes make people feel very thirsty
A drink bottle has the same shape as a crater
Gas in magma builds up pressure, like gas in the bottle
Magma tastes as sweet as a fizzy drink
questions.why: The magma holds gas like the bubbles in a fizzy drink, and pressure grows. A shaken bottle is a picture of that pressure.

questions.prompt: What is volcanic ash made of?
options: Tiny pieces of rock and glass
Small drops of cold water
Grey dust from old leaves
Soft pieces of burnt wood
questions.why: This ash is made of tiny pieces of rock and glass.

questions.prompt: How is one eruption different from another?
options: Some last for a year, and others never stop at all
Some are quiet with slow lava, and others are loud and sudden
Some happen under the snow, and others happen only at night
Some are made of water, and others are made of wind
questions.why: Some are quiet, with slow rivers of lava. Others are loud and sudden.

questions.prompt: Why do people near Merapi call the hot cloud a shaggy goat?
options: It runs down the mountain to find some grass
It makes a noise like a very large goat
Its curly grey shape looks like a goat's coat
Goats always run away when it comes near
questions.why: The text says they call it wedhus gembel, shaggy goat, because of its curly grey shape.

questions.prompt: Why was the summer after Tambora so cold in Europe?
options: Cold winds had blown in from the far north
Ash and gas blocked some of the sunlight
Winter had come early because of the moon
The eruption had moved Europe further north
questions.why: Tambora's ash and gas blocked some of the sunlight, and the next summer was very cold in Europe.

questions.prompt: What do volcanologists measure?
options: Tiny shakes in the ground and the gas in the air
The height of the trees and the number of birds
The colour of the lava and the taste of the ash
The speed of the wind and the depth of the sea
questions.why: They measure tiny shakes in the ground and the gas in the air.

chapters.title: Good Things from Fire
chapters.text:
Volcanoes can be dangerous, but they also give people good things. When ash and lava break down over many years, they turn into very rich soil. Plants grow well in this soil because it is full of minerals. That is why farmers on the slopes of volcanoes can grow rice, coffee, vegetables and tea. On the slopes of Merapi, farmers grow a sweet, scaly fruit called salak.

Volcanoes also heat water deep in the ground. The hot water comes up as hot springs. People can bathe in them, as they do at Ciater in West Java. Some countries, Indonesia among them, use the heat to make electricity.

Many visitors travel to see volcanoes such as Mount Bromo in East Java. They wake up early to watch the sunrise over its crater, and they cross a wide plain of grey volcanic sand called the Sea of Sand. Bromo is a special place for the people who live there, too. Each year, the Tengger people climb to the crater for a ceremony called Yadnya Kasada, and they bring gifts of fruit and vegetables.

At night, visitors to Kawah Ijen, also in East Java, can see something very strange. Burning gas in the crater makes bright blue flames.

questions.prompt: What happens to ash and lava over many years?
options: They turn into clean sand
They turn into hard ice
They turn into hot water
They turn into very rich soil
questions.why: When ash and lava break down over many years, they turn into very rich soil.

questions.prompt: Why do plants grow well in volcanic soil?
options: It stays wet all year
It is full of minerals
It is always warm at night
It has no stones in it
questions.why: Plants grow well in this soil because it is full of minerals.

questions.prompt: Which fruit grows on the slopes of Merapi?
options: Papaya
Apple
Salak
Mango
questions.why: On the slopes of Merapi, farmers grow a sweet, scaly fruit called salak.

questions.prompt: Where do hot springs get their heat?
options: From volcanoes heating water deep in the ground
From the sun shining on the water all day
From hot rain falling on the top of the mountain
From fires that people light beside the water
questions.why: Volcanoes heat water deep in the ground, and the hot water comes up as hot springs.

questions.prompt: What is the Sea of Sand?
options: A lake of water inside the crater of Bromo
A wide plain of grey volcanic sand near Bromo
A warm part of the sea around East Java
A beach where visitors watch the sunrise
questions.why: Visitors to Bromo cross a wide plain of grey volcanic sand called the Sea of Sand.

questions.prompt: What do the Tengger people bring to the crater for Yadnya Kasada?
options: Sacks of grey volcanic sand
Baskets of coffee and tea
Jars of water from hot springs
Gifts of fruit and vegetables
questions.why: Each year, the Tengger people climb to the crater and bring gifts of fruit and vegetables.

questions.prompt: Why is night a good time to visit Kawah Ijen?
options: The blue flames are easier to see in the dark
The Tengger ceremony happens there every night
The crater is too hot to visit in the day
The hot springs are open only after dark
questions.why: The text says visitors can see the bright blue flames at night, and bright flames stand out best when the sky is dark.

chapters.title: Staying Safe
chapters.text:
People who live near volcanoes learn how to stay safe. Scientists give each volcano an alert level. In Indonesia, there are four levels. Normal means the volcano is calm. Waspada means take care. Siaga means be ready. Awas, the highest level, means danger, and an eruption may be near.

When the level is high, officials ask families to leave. This is called evacuation. People take a bag with water, food and important papers. They go to a safe place far from the mountain. In villages near Merapi, a hollow wooden drum called a kentongan can pass on the warning from house to house.

Falling ash is a danger, too. It can hurt eyes and lungs. People wear masks and glasses, and they stay indoors when they can. They also sweep ash off their roofs, because a thick layer of it is very heavy.

Even after an eruption, rain can wash ash and rocks down the river valleys in a fast, thick flow. Lahar, the Javanese word for this flow, is now used by scientists all over the world.

When Merapi erupted strongly in 2010, warnings came early, and hundreds of thousands of people left in time. Good warnings save many lives.

questions.prompt: How many alert levels are there in Indonesia?
options: Three
Four
Two
Ten
questions.why: The text says that in Indonesia there are four levels.

questions.prompt: Which level tells people that the volcano is calm?
options: Awas
Waspada
Normal
Siaga
questions.why: Normal means the volcano is calm.

questions.prompt: What is it called when families leave because of danger?
options: Evacuation
Education
Eruption
Evaporation
questions.why: When the level is high, officials ask families to leave. This is called evacuation.

questions.prompt: What is a kentongan used for?
options: Carrying water to a safe place
Sweeping thick ash off the roofs
Measuring tiny shakes in the ground
Passing on a warning from house to house
questions.why: A hollow wooden drum called a kentongan can pass on the warning from house to house.

questions.prompt: Why do people sweep ash off their roofs?
options: The ash can start a fire on the roof
A thick layer of ash is very heavy
The ash stops the rain from falling
The ash makes the roof look very dirty
questions.why: They sweep ash off their roofs, because a thick layer of it is very heavy.

questions.prompt: Why must people stay careful even after an eruption has ended?
options: Lava can start to flow back up into the mountain
The alert level always goes up after an eruption ends
Rain can send a lahar of ash and rocks down the valleys
The masks and glasses stop working after a few days
questions.why: The text says that even after an eruption, rain can wash ash and rocks down the river valleys in a fast, thick flow called a lahar.

questions.prompt: What does the story of Merapi in 2010 show?
options: People near Merapi do not listen to warnings
Eruptions can be stopped by scientists
Merapi will never erupt strongly again
Early warnings help people to leave in time
questions.why: Warnings came early, and hundreds of thousands of people left in time. The text then says good warnings save many lives.
